proof: CALENDAR YEAR 2015 GROSS WAGES, PDF pages 206-211 of the FY2015 annual town report. Four printed columns -- SURNAME | FIRST NAME | DEPARTMENT | WAGES -- set as TWO side-by-side panels per page. LAYOUT READ OFF THE PAGE, NOT INFERRED (p206, pdfplumber points): left panel surname x0=73.64, first name x0=150.86, department x0=208.30, amount right-aligned at x1=314.18; right panel 349.12 / 426.33 / 475.73 / 573.60. Row pitch 14.88pt and every token of a printed line shares its `top` exactly. THE RUN PRINTS NO TOTAL ANYWHERE, so there is no arithmetic to close: this group is checked on COVERAGE and SEQUENCE, which prove the SHAPE and NOT the digits -- a misread digit survives both untouched. COVERAGE IS 100% ON EVERY PAGE, counted as money tokens on the page against records written: p206 46 printed lines, 92 money tokens, 92 records; p207 47/94/94; p208 47/94/94; p209 47/94/94; p210 47/94/94; p211 49/96/96. 564 names in total. Every single printed line yielded two complete records except the last two lines of p211, where the right panel has already ended, so there is no line on any page from which a record was refused. THE TWO PANELS ARE ONE LIST, AND THE DOCUMENT SAYS SO. They are read COLUMN-MAJOR -- the whole left panel of a page, then the whole right panel, then the next page -- and in that order the surname never goes backwards once in 564 rows. The discriminator is the page boundary, not the monotonicity: p206's right panel ends CAMPBELL and p207's LEFT panel opens CANTATORE, and p207's right ends FINCH while p208's left opens FINNEGAN. Two independent A-Z sequences -- which is what FY2016, FY2020 and FY2022 print and where merging would have been our claim rather than the town's -- cannot do that. Each panel read alone is also monotone, so monotonicity alone would not have settled it. THE LIST IS COMPLETE AT BOTH ENDS. p206 opens with ACKERMAN MEAGAN on its first printed line at top=41.49, with no column heading above it, and p205 carries only the divider `MISCELLANEOUS INFORMATION`; the run ends STRUBBE LAURIE (left) and ZRATE SEAN (right) on p211 and p212 is the meeting schedule. So unlike FY2016 -- whose list starts at BENOIT because the first page is not in the published report -- nothing is missing from the ends of this one. PAGE 208 IS A HOLE IN THE PAGE MAP and carries a full table of 94 records; it was never listed, while 206, 207, 209, 210 and 211 were. NO ROW IS PRINTED TWICE: 564 records, 564 distinct (surname, first name, department, amount) tuples. Every record carries a department. THE 564 PRINTED FIGURES SUM TO $17,363,978.82. That is the sum of what these six pages print and NOT a payroll total: the town prints no total here, the pages do not say what the figure includes, and nothing in the report reconciles it to an appropriation. It is also gross WAGES and not the cost of employing anybody.
